split_reasoning: Gathering and organizing information are steps in producing a study's information set, regardless of the source used.

parts.text: Gather and organize information about a problem or procedure for a study.
parts.type_reasoning: The organized information is a discrete input that an analyst or study team can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A study's assembled information set is a practical handoff, rather than each individual source collected.
parts.work_item: one organized information set for a study
parts.end: relevant information is collected and organized for analysis
parts.checked_by: the study team or lead analyst
parts.overlap_reasoning: Interviews and observations can supply this information, while analysis and study planning are related but distinct steps.

notes: The information set may be handed over incrementally in larger studies.

split_reasoning: Analyzing gathered data and developing alternatives are connected steps in producing solutions to a problem.

parts.text: Analyze gathered data and develop solutions or alternative methods of proceeding.
parts.type_reasoning: The analysis produces a set of options that management or the study team can consider.
parts.unit_reasoning: A set of alternatives for a defined problem is a usable output of the analysis, distinct from the final study documentation.
parts.work_item: one analysis and set of solution alternatives for a defined problem
parts.start: relevant study data are available for analysis
parts.end: analysis and alternatives are developed for review
parts.overlap_reasoning: Gathering supplies the data, while study documentation and form-change proposals can incorporate the analysis but have their own outputs.

split_reasoning: The target describes one continuing kind of interaction with personnel about implemented systems or procedures.

parts.text: Confer with personnel about the functioning of newly implemented systems or procedures.
parts.type_reasoning: The work described is consultation with personnel, with the value in the live interaction rather than a specified deliverable.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Records-program implementation may involve similar discussions, but neither statement is redundant with the other.

notes: Any subsequent corrective work or documentation would need separate coding if explicitly specified.

split_reasoning: Developing a records program, implementing its procedures, and checking compliance produce different outputs at different stages.

parts.text: Develop a records management program covering filing, protection, and retrieval.
parts.type_reasoning: Program development produces documented rules and procedures for organizational use.
parts.unit_reasoning: The program document is the management-level artifact reviewed and adopted as a whole.
parts.end: program rules and procedures are prepared for approval
parts.overlap_reasoning: The program may draw on study analysis and result in procedures documented in manuals, but those statements also cover other work.

parts.text: Implement a records management procedure in an organizational unit.
parts.type_reasoning: Implementation produces an operational procedure or configured records process for a unit.
parts.unit_reasoning: A procedure put into operation in a unit is a bounded implementation handoff rather than the whole program rollout.
parts.work_item: one records procedure put into operation in a unit
parts.start: approved records procedure and unit requirements are available
parts.end: procedure is put into use and handed over to responsible staff
parts.checked_by: unit management and records management staff
parts.overlap_reasoning: Implementation can include consultations or training, but those activities are also described independently.

parts.text: Review a unit's compliance with the records management program and report exceptions.
parts.type_reasoning: Compliance assurance is ongoing but produces discrete reviews and findings.
parts.unit_reasoning: One unit or scheduled review yields a set of findings that management can act on.
parts.start: unit or review period is selected for compliance checking
parts.end: compliance findings and exceptions are reported
parts.overlap_reasoning: No other statement specifically describes reviewing compliance with the records program.

notes: Shares and the implementation handoff vary with the scope and maturity of the records program.

split_reasoning: Reviewing forms and reports produces findings, while conferring with management and users is a distinct live activity.

parts.text: Review forms and reports for problems and potential improvements in format, distribution, and purpose.
parts.type_reasoning: A review produces findings about an existing form or report that others can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A form or report review is a bounded output that can feed a subsequent change proposal.
parts.work_item: one form or report review with identified problems and improvements
parts.start: form or report and its usage information are available for review
parts.end: review findings and possible improvements are recorded for consideration
parts.checked_by: management or the form or report owner
parts.overlap_reasoning: The review can inform the design and evaluation of changes, but it can also identify issues without producing an approved change.

parts.text: Confer with management and users about the format, distribution, and purpose of forms and reports.
parts.type_reasoning: The specified work is a live discussion to understand needs and problems.
parts.overlap_reasoning: These discussions gather information, but the broader information-gathering and personnel-interview tasks cover additional subjects and methods.

notes: The share of discussion varies with the number of users and stakeholders.

split_reasoning: Interviewing personnel and observing work on site are different activities, even though both inform the study.

parts.text: Interview personnel about unit functions, work, methods, equipment, and staffing.
parts.type_reasoning: The specified activity is a live interview with personnel to understand how work is performed.
parts.overlap_reasoning: The interview is one way of gathering study information and may cover the same users consulted about forms, but those tasks have broader or different scopes.

parts.text: Observe work on site to ascertain unit functions, methods, equipment, and staffing.
parts.type_reasoning: An observation produces recorded facts about work that the study team can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: One observation session's recorded findings form a bounded input to the study.
parts.start: observation session or work process is selected
parts.end: observations are recorded and available to the study team
parts.overlap_reasoning: Observation supplies information covered by the broader gathering task, but that task also includes other sources.

notes: On-site observation is not classified as physical work merely because it occurs away from a computer.

split_reasoning: Documenting findings and preparing implementation recommendations are parts of the same study deliverable.

parts.text: Document study findings and prepare recommendations for new systems, procedures, or organizational changes.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a study findings and recommendations document for management.
parts.unit_reasoning: The findings and recommendations are normally submitted together for a defined study or study phase.
parts.work_item: one study findings and recommendations report
parts.start: study findings and analysis are ready to document
parts.end: findings and implementation recommendations are submitted
parts.overlap_reasoning: Analysis develops alternatives that may appear in this report, while form and records recommendations can also be included but are separately scoped.

split_reasoning: Preparing manuals and training workers are different activities with different outputs.

parts.text: Prepare manuals for new forms, reports, procedures, or equipment in accordance with organizational policy.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a manual that workers and managers can use and review.
parts.unit_reasoning: A manual or issued manual section is the document handed over for use.
parts.work_item: one manual or issued manual section
parts.start: new process or equipment instructions and applicable policy are available
parts.end: manual or section is prepared and issued for use
parts.overlap_reasoning: A records management program may require documented procedures, but manuals also cover other forms, reports, and equipment.

parts.text: Train workers to use new forms, reports, procedures, or equipment in accordance with organizational policy.
parts.type_reasoning: Training is a live instructional interaction whose value is in workers learning the new practices.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Training can support records-program implementation, but it also covers other kinds of changes.

notes: The relative time spent on manuals and training depends on the rollout.

split_reasoning: Developing and recommending a change produces a proposal, while approving a change produces a separate decision.

parts.text: Design and evaluate changes to forms or reports and recommend a preferred change.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a proposed form or report change with an evaluation and recommendation.
parts.unit_reasoning: A proposal for a particular form or report is the unit submitted for a decision.
parts.work_item: one form or report change proposal
parts.start: a need or opportunity to change a form or report is identified
parts.end: proposed change and recommendation are submitted for review
parts.checked_by: form or report owner, users, or approving manager
parts.overlap_reasoning: Reviewing existing forms and developing study solutions can feed the proposal, while a study report can incorporate its recommendation.

parts.text: Approve a proposed change to a form or report.
parts.type_reasoning: Approval produces a recorded decision that the implementer relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each proposed change can be reviewed and signed off as a distinct decision.
parts.work_item: one form or report change approval decision
parts.start: change proposal is submitted for approval
parts.end: approval decision is recorded and communicated
parts.overlap_reasoning: Other statements may inform a decision, but none specifically describes approving a form or report change.

notes: Approval authority may belong to a different person from the analyst who designs the change.

split_reasoning: The listed subjects are alternative study topics; planning the study is one activity.

parts.text: Plan a study of an organizational work problem or procedure.
parts.type_reasoning: Planning produces a study approach that the study team and sponsor can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A plan for one defined study is the bounded output that guides subsequent work.
parts.work_item: one work-problem or procedures study plan
parts.start: study need or assignment is identified
parts.end: scope and study approach are prepared for review or use
parts.overlap_reasoning: Planning may include identifying needed information, but the separate gathering task covers the actual collection and organization.

split_reasoning: A storage equipment purchase recommendation and a space layout are distinct deliverables.

parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a purchase recommendation for a decision maker.
parts.unit_reasoning: A recommendation for a defined equipment need is submitted as a whole for purchasing consideration.
parts.start: storage requirements and constraints are identified
parts.overlap_reasoning: Equipment choices can support a records management program, but this recommendation is not limited to that program.

parts.text: Design an area layout to locate storage equipment within available space.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a layout that managers or facilities staff can review and use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A layout for a defined area is the artifact handed over for review and implementation.
parts.start: space dimensions, equipment, and placement requirements are available
parts.end: layout is prepared and submitted for review
parts.overlap_reasoning: The layout can support a records program, but it is a distinct space-planning output.

notes: Shares depend on whether equipment selection or space constraints require more analysis.
